day: # The Roman Lectionary for Mass: the Proper of Saints, as the Lectionary for
# Mass for use in the dioceses of the United States (second typical edition,
# 2002) gives it, from Felix Just's table at
# the maintainer, October 2026), checked against the USCCB's daily readings
# Given: the feasts that roman.csv does not have (Conversion of St. Paul to
# the Holy Innocents, 26-28 December), and the memorials and optional
# memorials the Lectionary gives proper readings for, wholly or in part
# (the Holy Name, Timothy and Titus, Joseph the Worker, Mary Mother of the
# Church, the Immaculate Heart, Barnabas, Martha, Mary and Lazarus, the
# Passion of John the Baptist, Our Lady of Sorrows, the Guardian Angels, the
# Dedication of the Basilicas of Peter and Paul), with the readings the
# Lectionary appoints from the Commons for the rest of the set.  Our Lady of
# Guadalupe is a feast with its own readings in the United States only.
# Not given: the memorials whose readings are all from the Commons, and Sts.
# Joachim and Anne, whose readings the Lectionary marks as chosen but not
# proper.  A feast that falls on a Sunday is not kept, so has no readings;
# on a memorial the weekday's readings are listed too.
# Keyed by the feasts' ids in data/Roman/feasts.csv.  Verses follow the New
# American Bible; a psalm's stanzas are joined where they run on, as in
# roman.csv.  The table's Rev 12:7-12a (Archangels) and Ps 124:7b-8 (Holy
# Innocents) are given as the USCCB prints them (docs/source-errors.csv).
